clue.text: Leaving party?

parts.note: reads like a farewell do for a departing colleague, but means quitting a political party

explanation.surface: A query about a send-off celebration for someone leaving work.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'leaving party' in Britain is a farewell gathering; the question mark warns that here it means walking out on a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Deserting one's political allegiance for another side is the classic act of desertion meant here.

clue.text: Singer needing most of seat?

indicators.note: most of says the word for seat loses its final letter

parts.note: a divan is a low couch or seat

explanation.surface: A performer who demands nearly all the chair to herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last letter N from DIVAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An operatic prima donna is a celebrated female singer.

clue.text: Beat current that's good for women

indicators.note: good for women means the letter for good takes the place of the letter for women

parts.note: a current is a flow of water or electricity

explanation.surface: A rhythm or electrical current claimed to benefit women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' signals swapping: the W in FLOW becomes G.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog someone is to beat them with a whip or stick.

clue.text: Accountant, politician and graduate teacher may find rest here

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
MP is a Member of Parliament
a BEd is a Bachelor of Education degree, held by a trained teacher

explanation.surface: Three professionals looking for somewhere to lie down.
explanation.walkthrough: BEd (Bachelor of Education) is the British teaching degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A folding cot used outdoors or for guests is a place to sleep or lie down.

clue.text: Stretch of water requiring popular permit

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
to let is to allow or permit

explanation.surface: A body of water that needs an approved licence.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow arm of the sea reaching into the land is a small stretch of water.

clue.text: Principal uniform worn by fighting men born on base

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after the preceding letters
worn by means the uniform letter goes inside, as clothing sits on a body
fighting suggests the letters of men and born are thrown into disorder

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A senior figure in uniform among soldiers born on a military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fighting men' looks like soldiers, but 'fighting' only scrambles the letters; 'base' is the mathematical constant e, a convention worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief or top person, the leader, is called by this phrase.

clue.text: A few heard leading review

indicators.note: heard says the word for a few is to be taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: some means a few
up means ahead or leading, as in a score

explanation.surface: Several people listening to the opening review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' turns SOME into its sound-alike SUM.
explanation.definitionFit: To summarise is to review the main points briefly.

clue.text: Used — and ate — nuts lightly fried

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone ate nuts that had been gently pan-cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like food but is the anagram signal for USED and ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Food cooked quickly in a little hot fat is cooked in this French manner.

clue.text: Partner accepting no site free for place to live

indicators.note: accepting means the partner word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a mate is a partner

indicators.note: free means the letters of no site are loosened and rearranged

explanation.surface: A spouse agreeing that no plot is free for their home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' looks like 'available' in the surface, but it signals rearranging the six letters of 'no site' before they go inside the partner word.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat on two floors of a house, with its own entrance, is a type of dwelling.

clue.text: Nice case of rivalry generating casual remark

parts.note: nice means pleasant

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside letters, first and last

explanation.surface: A friendly rivalry that prompts an offhand comment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' could be the French city; it is just the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A light, polite or joking comment made in conversation is this kind of remark.

clue.text: Sound of Queen once with low backing?

parts.note: VR is Victoria Regina, the cipher of Queen Victoria

indicators.note: backing means the word for low is read in reverse

parts.note: to low is to moo, as a cow does

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria with a deep-voiced backing singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' is the cow's call, not 'deep'; 'backing' reverses MOO to OOM.
explanation.definitionFit: This imitates the roar of an engine being revved, so it is a noise word.

clue.text: Car paint essentially must be in new emulsion

indicators.note: be in means the central letter sits inside the rearranged letters
new means the letters of emulsion are made into a fresh arrangement
essentially points to the core, the central letter of paint

explanation.surface: Decorating advice: the paint must be fresh emulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' gives I, the middle of PAINT; 'new' scrambles EMULSION; 'be in' places I within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A large luxurious chauffeur-driven saloon is a type of motor vehicle.

clue.text: Stroppy pros, to be sure, may be retrained

indicators.note: retrained means the letters are trained into a new order

explanation.surface: Bad-tempered professionals will certainly be sent back for training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrained' is the anagram signal for PROS TO BE SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisy and unruly behaviour is bad-tempered and awkward, which is the British sense of stroppy.

clue.text: Criminal type who might hold up a store

definitions.text: Criminal type who might hold up a store

parts.words: Criminal type who might hold up a store
parts.note: hold up suggests armed robbery, but it means lifting goods from a shop

explanation.surface: A description of a robber who raids a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold up' reads as an armed robbery; here it means literally lifting up the goods in a store.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief who takes goods from a shop without paying is this kind of offender.

clue.text: Revealing close call supporting United?

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed beneath the other part

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names
a near thing is a narrow escape or close call

explanation.surface: A narrow escape for a football club, perhaps Manchester United.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts NEAR THING below U in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Digging up or bringing to light something hidden is a way of exposing it.

clue.text: Suspend setter for such an expression?

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing a look, as in a guilty or shamefaced face

parts.note: to hang is to suspend
a setter is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A crossword setter suspended, so looking sheepish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the crossword compiler but is the gun dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A shamefaced, guilty look is the kind of face this adjective describes.

clue.text: Guest gutted about landlord with private place that's empty

indicators.note: about means the outer pair goes around the landlord word
gutted means the inside letters are removed, leaving the outside pair

parts.note: a host is a landlord, as of a pub
own means private or personal, as in your own room

explanation.surface: A guest's room cleared out around the landlord's private quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' sounds like emotional distress, but here it empties a word of its inside letters; a pub landlord is a host in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A settlement abandoned by its inhabitants is a deserted, lifeless town.

clue.text: Fancy a blonde, mate?

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A friend asking his pal if he is attracted to a fair-haired woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' reads as 'be attracted to' but is the anagram signal. The answer is a dated British upper-class way to address a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A jovial old-fashioned form of address for a male friend is a term for a pal.

clue.text: Layer seen in ozone hole reversed

indicators.note: reversed says the found letters are read backwards
seen in means the letters are found within the words ozone hole

explanation.surface: An atmospheric layer observed around the hole in the ozone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layer' looks like a stratum of the atmosphere, but it means a bird that lays eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A female chicken that produces eggs is literally an egg-layer.

clue.text: Identify personal problem offering hopeful treatment

parts.note: to place someone is to identify or recognise them
BO is body odour, a personal hygiene problem

explanation.surface: Diagnosing a private problem and offering a cure.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy pill given in the hope it helps through belief alone is an inert remedy.

clue.text: Not a sound will be heard out of this!

definitions.text: Not a sound will be heard out of this!

parts.words: Not a sound will be heard out of this!
parts.note: sounds like a demand for silence, but describes the range beyond which nothing can be heard

explanation.surface: A stern order that nobody should make any noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of this' means beyond its range, not 'from this source'.
explanation.definitionFit: The distance within which one can catch sounds; outside it nothing reaches the listener.

clue.text: Horse always found around hospital department

indicators.note: found around means the always word sits around the other letters

parts.note: ever means always
ENT is ear, nose and throat, a hospital department

explanation.surface: A horse always turning up near a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer can be the rider too, but the competition horse is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse trained for three-day equestrian competitions is a type of competition horse.

clue.text: Contacted regulars of team and suffered

indicators.note: regulars means every other letter, taken at regular intervals

parts.note: ailed means was ill, suffered

explanation.surface: A team's regular players were contacted and had a bad time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regulars of' takes the even letters E and M of team.
explanation.definitionFit: Sending an electronic message to someone is a way of getting in touch.

clue.text: Lost all interest with the onset of rows between stars

indicators.note: lost means the letters of all interest have gone astray into a new order
onset is the beginning, so the first letter of rows

explanation.surface: Someone bored by the start of arguments among celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' tempts as celebrities, and 'rows' as quarrels.
explanation.definitionFit: Space lying among the stars of a galaxy is described with this adjective.

clue.text: City shelter dropouts left empty

parts.note: lee is shelter from the wind

indicators.note: left empty means the inside of dropouts is cleared, keeping its outer letters

explanation.surface: A town's refuge abandoned by its drifters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large city in West Yorkshire, northern England.

clue.text: Somewhat undervalued fuel

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the word undervalued is used

explanation.surface: A complaint that fuel is priced too low.
explanation.walkthrough: It is the British name for diesel for road vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Diesel oil for lorries and cars goes by this British name.

clue.text: Drink made from bananas, full of energy

indicators.note: full of means the energy letter fills the middle of the other word

parts.note: bananas is slang for mad
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A beverage brewed from bananas, giving a boost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' reads as fruit but means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcoholic beverage fermented from honey and water is an old drink.

clue.text: Part of leg that may be off in steak

indicators.note: in means the off word sits inside the steak word

parts.note: a T-bone is a cut of steak
high means gone off, of meat

explanation.surface: A cut of the leg that could have gone bad in a steak.
explanation.definitionFit: The femur, the bone of the upper limb, is a component of the leg.

clue.text: Lord once kept in privilege illegally rejected

indicators.note: rejected says the hidden letters are read backwards
kept in signals the letters are held inside the words privilege illegally

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A former nobleman held on to privileges unlawfully.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'kept' in the definition, but 'kept in' is the signal that the letters are held inside 'privilege illegally'; 'rejected' then reverses EGEIL.
explanation.definitionFit: In feudal times this was a superior to whom service and allegiance were owed, a master.

clue.text: Utter prerogative

definitions.meaning: complete or absolute, as in a proper idiot

explanation.surface: Speak your privilege out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially an absolute fool is called this kind of fool; also an entitlement one holds.

clue.text: So indeed, desperately holding Victor, fell sharply

indicators.note: holding means the scrambled letters contain the Victor letter
desperately means wildly, so the letters of so indeed are scrambled

parts.note: V is Victor in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An agreement that a man named Victor took a steep fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperately' scrambles SO INDEED; 'holding' puts V inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Plunging steeply, like an aircraft heading downward, is a sudden drop.
